purpose: Runtime identities for every execution cell used in Phase A, and the provenance of the provisioned Node 22 runtime.
note: Timestamps are deliberately omitted: this package must be byte-reproducible. Ordering is established by git history.

provisionedRuntime.globalMutation: none; extracted to a scratch path and invoked by absolute path. Global node remained v25.0.0 and global npm remained 11.6.2, verified before and after.
provisionedRuntime.limitation: Windows MAX_PATH forced relocation to a short root. This is an environment constraint of the audit host, not a repository defect.

prediction: npm ci would FAIL under npm 10 because package.json:50-52 declares overrides.postcss while package-lock.json contains no overrides key.
observed: npm ci succeeded (exit 0) in all four cells. The prediction was REFUTED.
conclusion: CLAUDE.md:105 npm-10 compatibility is CONFIRMED for installation. The design is fully crossed: npm test outcome depends solely on the Node axis; the npm axis has no effect.

lockfileTamperCheck.rationale: Any lockfile rewrite under npm 11 would silently revert commit 0c73d94. README.md:23 instructs `npm install`, which would do exactly that.

uncertainty: Only Node 22.13.1 and 25.0.0 were tested. The boundary version at which artifact identity changes is UNKNOWN and lies somewhere in 22.13.1 < v <= 25.0.0.
alternativeExplanation: npm-version effects were excluded by testing both npm majors against both Node majors; no npm-attributable difference was observed.
independentlyReproduced: Within this audit only: three consecutive runs per Node version produced identical results. Not reproduced on a second machine.
